answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable deposit in a vault before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. A prism of independent validators checks whether the agent completed a randomly assigned task, while a public thread links its deposit, submissions, and outcomes over time. Creating many identities then requires funding each one, and failed or duplicate work risks losing those deposits; the attacker pays real capital and validation costs rather than gaining influence by naming alone.
